skill.name: product-demand-evidence
skill.description: Research product demand using supplied discussions or SocialDataX searches, with source-linked pain points, alternatives, purchase concerns, and counterevidence.
skill.summary: Turn public discussions into a bounded product demand brief with traceable evidence and next-step validation questions.
skill.author: devinchen2014

security_audit.summary: All 42 static alerts are false positives: Markdown formatting, service links, credential configuration guidance, and readable Chinese prose explain the matches. Two semantic risks remain: automatic execution of an unpinned npm package and mandatory propagation of token-bearing XHS URLs. No evidence found of embedded credentials, encoded payloads, or instructions to override the audit.

remediation.issue: Direct CLI examples automatically execute socialdatax-skills@latest through npx.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed package version and lock dependencies with integrity hashes. Obtain approval before installation and restrict the process to task-required credentials.

remediation.issue: The citation rule requires exposing xsec_token parameters in every display, storage, and forwarding context.
remediation.suggestion: Keep token-bearing URLs only in authorized retrieval contexts. Use source IDs or safe citations elsewhere, and require approval before sharing full token-bearing links.

content.user_title: Validate Product Demand with Sourced Discussions
content.value_statement: Product ideas often rely on assumptions about customer needs and willingness to pay. This skill organizes public discussions into traceable evidence, counterevidence, and focused validation questions.
actual_capabilities: Analyze supplied posts and comments without requiring online access or an API key.
Guide bounded searches, detail retrieval, and main-comment collection across Xiaohongshu, Douyin, and Baidu Tieba through SocialDataX.
Separate pain points, existing alternatives, purchase concerns, explicit intent, and counterevidence using quotations and source references.
Deduplicate evidence by platform and content ID while flagging repeated authors, repeated experiences, and promotional material.
Report research coverage, incomplete retrieval, audience fit, unknowns, and up to three follow-up validation suggestions.
Distinguish observed facts, participant quotations, and analysis without treating engagement counts as customer demand.
limitations: Online retrieval depends on SocialDataX authentication, service availability, platform coverage, and available paid credits.
Direct CLI use requires Node.js and npm; examples execute an unpinned package, and source-link instructions retain XHS tokens.
Default coverage allows two platforms, two one-page queries each, and detail plus main comments for four posts; replies are excluded.
Public discussions cannot establish market size, verified purchases, conversion rates, or product success.

use_cases.title: Test an Early Product Hypothesis
use_cases.description: Compare an initial product idea against relevant complaints, existing workarounds, and evidence that the problem is already adequately solved.

use_cases.title: Investigate Purchase Objections
use_cases.description: Organize discussion evidence about price, reliability, alternatives, and audience fit before choosing a feature or positioning experiment.

use_cases.title: Prepare Evidence-Based Interviews
use_cases.description: Review supplied discussion records, identify contradictory accounts, and generate focused interview questions for unresolved customer assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Review Supplied Discussions
prompt_templates.prompt: Use product-demand-evidence to analyze these posts: [materials]. My idea is [idea] for [audience]. Identify pain points, alternatives, concerns, and counterevidence. Do not browse.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: analyze existing material without online setup.

prompt_templates.title: Research a Product Idea
prompt_templates.prompt: Research [idea] for [audience] using the default sample limits on [two supported platforms]. Report queries, dates, quotations, sources, and gaps. Separate evidence from interpretation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: conduct bounded online discovery with configured SocialDataX access.

prompt_templates.title: Challenge a Demand Assumption
prompt_templates.prompt: Test the assumption [assumption] for [audience]. Seek complaints and evidence that alternatives are sufficient. Deduplicate sources and separate willingness-to-pay statements from general interest.
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced: actively seek evidence against a product hypothesis.

prompt_templates.title: Extend an Incomplete Research Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Continue this brief: [brief and retrieval state]. Investigate [unknown] with an additional cap of [sample limit]. Preserve deduplication and pagination state. Propose three validation steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: extend prior research without repeating retrieval or inflating evidence counts.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: Assess a cleaning device using supplied discussions from renters.
output: Illustrative structure only; no real participant evidence is claimed.
Coverage: supplied material only; no additional search performed.
Evidence table: source reference, audience fit, quotation, pain point, workaround, objection, and supporting or opposing evidence.
Decision brief: supported assumptions, weakened assumptions, unknowns, and up to three validation questions.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: Evaluate willingness to pay when retrieval returns only promotional posts.
output: Evidence status: the available material is promotional and does not establish independent customer demand.
Willingness to pay: unknown; engagement counts do not demonstrate purchase intent.
Next step: interview target users about their current alternative and a concrete purchasing decision.

best_practices: Define the target audience and a falsifiable research question before selecting platforms or queries.
Provide original sources and preserve deduplication records; separate quotations, observations, and interpretations.
Confirm online costs and sample limits; review package versions and token-bearing links before execution or sharing.
anti_patterns: Treating likes, views, comments, or repeated promotional posts as independent evidence of paying customers.
Expanding platforms or pagination without explicit sample limits, or hiding failed and incomplete retrieval.
Presenting hypothetical examples, inferred identities, or unsupported market estimates as observed research results.

faq.question: Do I need an API key?
faq.answer: Supplied-material analysis needs no key. Direct online CLI calls need a configured SocialDataX key; an authenticated hosted MCP connection uses its existing authentication.

faq.question: Which platforms are supported?
faq.answer: The workflow lists Xiaohongshu, Douyin, and Baidu Tieba. It uses at most two platforms by default.

faq.question: What does the default sample include?
faq.answer: Each platform gets two one-page queries with up to ten candidates each. Four posts total receive details and up to twenty main comments each.

faq.question: Can this prove that customers will pay?
faq.answer: No. It distinguishes explicit price or purchase statements from general complaints, but cannot verify transactions, conversion rates, or market size.

faq.question: Does it publish content or contact people?
faq.answer: The documented workflow retrieves and analyzes data. It does not log into social accounts, publish, comment, send messages, or contact interview participants.

faq.question: What should I review before online use?
faq.answer: Online requests may consume paid credits. Review unpinned npm execution and token-bearing source links; keep API keys out of chat and logs.
